methods.label: Apply the negative-exponent rule
methods.explanation:
For a nonzero base, a negative exponent means taking the reciprocal of the corresponding positive power. Thus
\[
(-2)^{-2}=\frac{1}{(-2)^2}=\frac14.
\]
Evaluate this power before subtracting:
\[
2-(-2)^{-2}=2-\frac14=\boxed{\frac74},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only negative integer exponents, the sign of an even power, and elementary fraction subtraction are required.

review.mathematicalCheck: The base is nonzero, so (−2)^(−2)=1/(−2)²=1/4. Evaluating the power first gives 2−1/4=7/4.
